anchors.description: Horizontal outer-frame width of the bottom-right arched window, between the outer left and outer right window-frame edges at the same height (row y~570-573 px).
anchors.visible_evidence: The window frame outer edges are the dark boundaries flanking both endpoints: sub-pixel threshold crossings give left outer edge x=1069.4 at y=573 and right outer edge x=1225.0 at y=570, i.e. 155.6 px between outer frame edges. The same sunlit wall beside the window carries a regular Flemish-bond brick lattice: 18 bed-joint courses over 124 px (pitch 6.89 px), header module 12.5 px, stretcher module 24.75 px, with stretcher/header = 1.98 as required for a brick laid length = 2x width + joint. Using a 210x100x50 mm brick with ~10-12 mm joints (modules 62/112/222 mm) all three directions agree on 8.96-9.00 mm/px and imply cos(theta)=1.00, i.e. a fronto-parallel wall, so horizontal pixels convert directly.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The brick format is inferred, not read off a label. Only the Dutch Waal/klinker 210x100x50 format reproduces the measured bed:header:stretcher module ratio (62:112:222) with zero yaw; a thicker German Reichsformat 240x115x63 would require an impossible foreshortening factor cos>1. Residual scale uncertainty about +/-8%. The two candidate endpoints sit roughly 1-3 px outside the true frame outer edges, so the reported span (160.0 px) slightly exceeds the exact outer-frame width (155.6 px, about 1.40 m).
